<p>“Ah… my head…”</p><p>I opened my eyes on the sofa and sat up, looking at the air conditioner.</p><p>The panties and shorts hanging on the hanger beneath it proved that yesterday hadn’t been a dream.</p><p>“Huu.”</p><p>I closed my eyes, took a deep breath, then turned my head to look at the bed.</p><p>“As I thought…”</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="290735" loading="lazy">
</p><p>Min Se-rin was fast asleep on the bed, breathing softly.</p><p>‘I went through all that trouble to put the robe on her, and now she’s taken it off again.’</p><p>Noticing the empty water bottle I’d left by her bedside before going to sleep, it seemed she’d woken up at some point to drink.</p><p>I moved as quietly as possible, carefully gathering my clothes and putting them on.</p><p>I’d have to explain everything that happened today eventually, but not now.</p><p>If I was going to do it, I wanted to avoid this situation for now, get a good night’s rest, and talk to her tomorrow.</p><p>‘I think I slept about eight hours too. Se-rin must’ve been really exhausted…’</p><p>I closed the window for the sleeping Min Se-rin before leaving the room.</p><p>In front of the door was a wagon filled with food.</p><p>When I lifted the silver lid, I found cold soup and bread inside.</p><p>‘I guess they rang the bell, got no answer, and just left it here…’</p><p>In the end, I sighed and took the elevator down to the first floor.</p><p>‘Good thing I did laundry and showered before bed last night…’</p><p>Last night had been a perfect example of just how harmful alcohol could be to a person.</p><p>Both Min Se-rin and I had been drunk, and we’d created a memory that would live in infamy for the rest of our lives.</p><p>I closed my eyes and shook my head, trying not to think about it.</p><p>Ding—</p><p>After arriving on the first floor, I stepped out into the lobby and looked around.</p><p>‘Where was it again…’</p><p>I was sure there had been a café-style lounge area on the first floor when I first arrived at this hotel.</p><p>“Over there.”</p><p>I spotted a lounge area where several people in suits were sitting in chairs, drinking coffee.</p><p>I made my way over, took a seat in the corner, and watched as people helped themselves to coffee from the fridge.</p><p>Of course, the café wasn’t actually open, so they must’ve set it up like this as a workaround.</p><p>I walked over to the fridge, grabbed a cold black coffee and a bottle of water, then returned to my seat.</p><p>With no phone and no friends, I couldn’t sit and chat with acquaintances like the other Hunters. I just stared blankly into space, sipping my coffee.</p><p>‘I’m hungry… Do I have to wait until lunch?’</p><p>It was almost noon, and lunch wouldn’t arrive until 1:30 PM.</p><p>But even if he went up to the room at 1:30, Min Se-rin would probably still be asleep.</p><p>He was bored, but it wasn’t unbearable.</p><p>‘There was something I had to do after this…’</p><p>He passed the time imagining how he’d screw over the handler after the mission ended.</p><p>‘For something Lee Seung-jun said was dangerous, it’s been surprisingly quiet until now…’</p><p>Still, he couldn’t forgive the handler.</p><p>His memories were hazy, but last night, while he and Min Se-rin were drunk on Dropz, she’d definitely said that even if they requested help, most would refuse, that they’d have to send trustworthy Hunters, that most of the security personnel were Hunters sent on the Association President’s orders, and that it was politically sensitive within the Association—so even among the Hunters personally designated by the President, some had turned it down.</p><p>‘The more I think about it, the angrier I get…’</p><p>***</p><p>2:30 PM.</p><p>He’d sat in the café for nearly three hours, lost in his own thoughts.</p><p>His stomach was now loudly protesting, demanding he stop drinking coffee and put something with actual nutrients into his body.</p><p>‘It should be gone by now… right?’</p><p>He stood up and headed for the elevator.</p><p>Praying it would be gone, he took the elevator and arrived in front of the door.</p><p>‘What the… why isn’t it here?’</p><p>The wagon was nowhere to be seen.</p><p>‘Is today a no-lunch day? Or… did Min Se-rin eat it?’</p><p>He pressed his ear to the door, but there was no sign of anyone inside.</p><p>Cautiously, he swiped his card and entered the room.</p><p>“Oh…”</p><p>The once-messy room was now spotless.</p><p>He wondered if a staff member had cleaned it or if Min Se-rin had, but the table gave it away—she’d tidied up and left.</p><p>On the table was a neatly arranged meal and a Post-it note.</p><p>『Seong-hyeon-ssi, I’m sorry. I caused you so much trouble. I cleaned up the mess from yesterday. I’m really sorry…』</p><p>The hastily scribbled note was so rushed it almost made him laugh.</p><p>“At least she’s got manners.”</p><p>He lifted the lid of the first dish to find a mouthwatering bowl of pollack soup.</p><p>‘This is it.’</p><p>Today’s lunch seemed to be Korean cuisine.</p><p>He immediately microwaved the rice and pollack soup.</p><p>As he took his first spoonful of the steaming broth, a jolt of flavor shot through him.</p><p>‘So that’s why drunks crave broth the morning after…’</p><p>Before I knew it, I’d tossed my spoon aside and was chugging the soup straight from the bowl.</p><p>***</p><p>“Huuu…”</p><p>I sat on the edge of the bed in my suit, taking deep breaths.</p><p>Yesterday, I’d spent the entire day lying in bed to rest.</p><p>My body had fully recovered, but the problem was that in ten minutes, when I walked out that door, I’d have to face Min Se-rin again.</p><p>‘Maybe I should’ve just let it all out yesterday.’</p><p>Regret washed over me for putting it off, but there was nothing I could do now. I put on my shoes, clipped on my walkie-talkie, and stepped out the door.</p><p>When I reached the 14th floor and exited the elevator, Min Se-rin was standing right there.</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="290736" loading="lazy">
</p><p>“…”</p><p>We stared at each other in silence, neither of us able to speak first.</p><p>Min Se-rin averted her eyes within a second, her face flushing red.</p><p>I had no idea how much she remembered from the day before yesterday, but the way she looked so embarrassed suggested she might recall things she shouldn’t.</p><p>‘If I don’t say anything now, this is going to get *really* awkward…’</p><p>I steeled my resolve and forced a smile, greeting her as if nothing had happened.</p><p>“Se-rin, you’re here early.”</p><p>“Huh? Oh, yes! I left a little early!”</p><p>Min Se-rin seemed to pick up on my unspoken intention to pretend yesterday never happened. She quickly smiled back and replied.</p><p>‘Phew… pulled it off.’</p><p>Thankfully, the worst-case scenario had been avoided.</p><p>Min Se-rin and I patrolled as usual, chatting about this and that.</p><p>We both seemed to be avoiding any topics related to that day—alcohol, Baekgwang Construction, anything that might bring it up. The conversation stuck strictly to other subjects.</p><p>‘Now that I think about it…’</p><p>Min Se-rin’s condition had improved dramatically.</p><p>On the first day, she’d looked like she might collapse at any moment, and the day before yesterday, she’d been in such rough shape it was hard to even call her human.</p><p>She’d been beyond exhausted—more like she belonged in a coffin. But now, while she still looked a little worn out, her condition was incomparably better than before.</p><p>“Se-rin, you must’ve slept well. You look a lot better.”</p><p>I was in such a good mood that I ended up saying it out loud.</p><p>‘Ah, fuck….’</p><p>I always knew I was an idiot, but I never thought it was this bad.</p><p>“Ah, so what I meant was…”</p><p>I frantically tried to cover up my mistake, but the moment I turned my head and saw Min Se-rin, my words died in my throat.</p><p>‘I’m so screwed.’</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="290737" loading="lazy">
</p><p>Min Se-rin’s face was a mix of shock and bewilderment.</p><p>It was obvious she was thinking, *What the hell is this guy doing?*</p><p>I had already implicitly demanded we keep that incident a secret, and now I was the one bringing it up in conversation.</p><p>“···.”</p><p>In the end, the two of us patrolled in silence for hours.</p><p>As I cursed myself and wallowed in self-loathing, Min Se-rin finally spoke up after hours of silence.</p><p>“Seong-hyeon-ssi… do you remember what happened the day before yesterday?”</p><p>This was my chance.</p><p>The last opportunity heaven had given me. I fidgeted with my tie unnecessarily and put on a slightly surprised expression before answering.</p><p>“Huh? Oh, that… I actually don’t remember much after Se-rin-ssi finished that last bottle and drank it. Did I do something wrong?”</p><p>Min Se-rin’s expression brightened for a moment before she quickly regained her composure and said,</p><p>“I… I don’t really remember either… I think I made a huge mistake. When I woke up, you were gone, and I was only in my underwear, asleep in your bed… Do you remember where you slept?”</p><p>“I… slept on the sofa. Honestly, I don’t even remember how I got there. When I woke up, you were wearing a robe… Did you move me to the sofa while I was asleep?”</p><p>“Ah! Now that you mention it, there was a robe thrown on the floor when I woke up… I don’t remember much either, but I think I must have moved you.”</p><p>Yes.</p><p>I had finally turned this fucked-up situation around.</p><p>My self-deprecation quickly turned into self-praise.</p><p>‘Yoon Seong-hyeon, you genius bastard.’</p><p>Min Se-rin turned toward me, bending at a 120-degree angle, and said,</p><p>“I’m so sorry! I must have been such an embarrassment…”</p><p>“No, it’s fine. I don’t remember much after that last bottle, but it was fun drinking after so long. Please, don’t do that…”</p><p>Min Se-rin didn’t straighten up even after my response.</p><p>I kept emphasizing, “I really don’t remember anything after that last bottle.”</p><p>“If Se-rin-ssi is going to apologize, then so will I. I’m sorry for passing out first!”</p><p>I bowed my head just like her, and Min Se-rin panicked, grabbing my arm and forcing me to straighten up.</p><p>“Seong-hyeon, why are you acting like this…! Just—ah, fine. I won’t apologize either.”</p><p>“Yes. Then that’s settled.”</p><p>When I lifted my head, Min Se-rin was smiling.</p><p>‘Phew…’</p><p>It felt like a heavy weight had been lifted from my mind.</p><p>‘Just need to watch my mouth for the next two days.’</p><p>After that, Min Se-rin and I had a pleasant conversation for several hours.</p><p>We even talked about that day.</p><p>Of course, only up until the last bottle.</p><p>“There’s… something I’m curious about.”</p><p>“Yes, Seong-hyeon, go ahead.”</p><p>I asked Min Se-rin the question I’d been agonizing over alone yesterday.</p><p>“You remember my handler, right?”</p><p>“Yes, I… do remember that.”</p><p>“So, when I get back, I’m planning to change my handler right away. Do you think the Association would let me assign someone from my family to the role?”</p><p>“Of course.”</p><p>I cheered internally. I could fire that crazy bitch immediately and assign Na-hyeon as my handler—it’d be a win-win for both of us.</p><p>“But…”</p><p>“Yes?”</p><p>“Are you… planning to assign your older sister, the one who just joined Central HQ, as your handler?”</p><p>“Ah, yes…”</p><p>My excitement vanished in an instant.</p><p>I had a bad feeling about what Min Se-rin was about to say, even without hearing it.</p><p>“To become a handler, even if they’re family, they need at least a year of experience as a staff member… Since she just started, she’ll have a six-month probation period, and even after that, she’ll need another year of experience. So, for at least a year and a half, you won’t be able to assign her, even as family…”</p><p>“Ah… thank you.”</p><p>I was furious at the fact that even as an A-rank, I couldn’t just pick whoever I wanted as my handler. I’d have to roll the gacha again at random.</p><p>‘What’s the point of being A-rank if I can’t even choose my own handler? No wonder they get assassination attempts with this kind of management.’</p><p>As I was muttering baseless complaints about the Association in my head, a loud noise shook the hotel lightly.</p><p>Boom—</p><p>“Huh?”</p><p>“What the…”</p><p>Min Se-rin and I stared at each other in shock when a voice crackled over the radio.</p><p>-Terrorist detected on the 16th floor. Immediate backup requested.</p><p>Min Se-rin and I nodded and bolted for the stairs.</p>
